learn.title: One answer for every expression
learn.body: What is $2+3\times 4$? If you add first you get 20; if you multiply first you get 14. To make sure everyone gets the same answer, mathematicians agreed on an order. The correct answer is 14.

learn.title: The order
learn.body: 1. Brackets first. 2. Exponents. 3. Multiplication and division, left to right. 4. Addition and subtraction, left to right. Multiplication and division share a step, and so do addition and subtraction.

learn.title: Work out $6+2^3\times 2$
learn.body: Follow the order one level at a time.

learn.title: Left to right
learn.body: When operations share a step, go left to right. $18\div 3\times 2$ is $6\times 2=12$, not $18\div 6=3$. Likewise $10-2+1=9$, not 7.

learn.title: Work out $20-(3+2)^2\div 5$
learn.body: Brackets, then exponent, then divide, then subtract.
Brackets can override the order: $(2+3)\times 4=20$. Use them to show what to do first.

questions.explanation: Division and multiplication go left to right: $18\div 3=6$, then $6\times 2=12$.

questions.prompt: In $(8-2)\times 3^2$, the first step is to work out \_\_.
Work out $10-2\times 3+1$. Put the steps in order.
questions.explanation: Multiplication comes first. Then subtract and add from left to right.

questions.prompt: Match each expression with its value.
questions.explanation: Apply brackets, then exponents, then multiplication or division, then addition or subtraction.
